description: The bar chart, titled “Targets (conceptualized or operationalized) over time,” illustrates the distribution of target categories across years from 2012 to 2022, based on a systematic review of hateful communication datasets. The horizontal axis represents the year, while the vertical axis is scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, indicating the normalized proportion of targets per year (likely representing the share of datasets or instances that conceptualized or operationalized each target category). Each stacked bar corresponds to a year and is segmented by target count categories: 0 (blue), 1 (orange), 2–4 (green), 5–7 (red), and 8+ (purple), as defined in the legend. In 2012 and 2013, nearly all targets fall into the “2–4” and “0” categories respectively, with 2012 entirely green (2–4) and 2013 entirely blue (0). From 2014 onward, the bars become increasingly segmented, showing growing diversity in target counts. For example, 2016 shows a large blue segment (0), followed by orange (1) and green (2–4); by 2019, red (5–7) and purple (8+) segments appear, indicating more datasets with higher numbers of targets. In 2022, the bar is the most diversified, with substantial contributions from all categories, including the largest purple (8+) segment observed in the chart. The chart visually conveys a trend toward increasing complexity and multiplicity in the conceptualization of targets in hateful communication research over time.
